owner_creation.analysis: The prompt_col c_int owns the display width of the prompt prefix; clear_cmd zeroes it and cmd_putstr adds measured character widths while emitting prompt text.
owner_creation.invariant: Prompt width is metadata, not an owned prompt buffer.

aliases_escapes.analysis: Cursor/home/scroll routines use prompt_col as the left editing boundary; no borrow of the actual prompt bytes is retained in this number.
aliases_escapes.invariant: A copied width cannot extend prompt-text lifetime.

callback_targets.analysis: cmd_putstr invokes putchr while measuring prompt_col; the width value does not own or store the terminal provider callback.
callback_targets.invariant: Width metadata and native output callbacks are separate.

invalidation.analysis: Redrawing a prompt replaces prompt_col’s boundary while a saved cmd_col/cp may still describe the previous prompt layout.
invalidation.invariant: Prompt replacement invalidates old column relationships.
limitations: The specific condition is prompt_col changing while a saved cmd_col/cp pair still describes the old layout; bounds rely on coherence.

mutation_commit.analysis: cmd_putstr increments cmd_col and prompt_col after output, and clear_cmd assigns them separately; no failure-atomic display-state object commits them together.
mutation_commit.invariant: Prompt and cursor widths must be updated coherently.

release_pair.analysis: The prompt_col scalar is never freed and does not own the prompt string returned by other modules; ending prompt display releases no text through this field.
release_pair.invariant: Width retirement cannot free a prompt-data owner.

error_cleanup.analysis: Failed output or unsuitable terminal geometry does not roll back width accumulation here; callers must not infer a rendered prefix solely from prompt_col.
error_cleanup.invariant: Recorded width is not proof of successful rendering.

signals_handoff.analysis: The global is part of raw command/display state accessed by exported functions, with no handler-exclusion contract encoded by prompt_col's type.
limitations: Source-specific review of coupled legacy editor state; M0-MEM-001 remains open and no new runtime defect is asserted from raw-pointer structure alone.
